Total revenue across the analysis period reached $2,286,031 with an overall profit margin of 32.9%, generating $751,288 in profit.

Furniture is the leading product category, contributing $1,219,910 (53.4% of total revenue), followed by Electronics and Office Supplies. Grocery is the lowest-performing category and is a candidate for a promotional push or portfolio review.
The single best-selling product is 'Sofa 3-Seater', generating $253,179 in revenue. The top 3 products together account for $650,008 in revenue, indicating some concentration risk worth monitoring.
West is the strongest region, driving 27.9% of total revenue.
Corporate is the highest-value customer segment by revenue ($801,874), suggesting marketing and retention budget should be weighted toward this group.
Repeat customers make up 99.4% of the customer base -- growing this rate has an outsized impact on revenue stability since repeat customers are cheaper to serve than new-customer acquisition.
Sunday is the peak order day of the week, useful for scheduling promotions, staffing, and ad spend timing.
Higher discount levels (>15%) are associated with thinner or negative profit margins in the data, so discounting strategy should be reviewed per category rather than applied uniformly.
The return rate is 1.5% of line items -- within a normal retail range but worth tracking over time as a leading indicator of product-quality or fulfillment issues.
